title: Request Chronograph: per-symbol latency reconciliation and KV prefetch amortization
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: build a lightweight, per-request "chronograph" that reconstructs the micro-timeline for each token/subtoken emission and amortizes KV prefetch costs across the request. Unlike prior work that focuses on aggregated per-token probes, this ticket implements request-scoped reconciliation so we can answer: (1) which subtokens paid for KV prefetching, (2) how much compute vs KV latency contributed to tail SLOs, and (3) how to credit/debit cached prefixes across batched requests. This supports cost chargebacks, SLA debugging, and smarter prefetch policies.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: every request emitted has a chronograph span that groups per-layer and per-subtoken spans with the fields in emitted_trace_fields
KV amortization: a reproducible algorithm assigns prefetch cost to a deterministic set of subtokens and matches offline accounting within 2% for synthetic workloads
Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard shows per-request micro-timelines, 95th/99th tail attribution breakdown (compute vs KV vs queue), and aggregated monthly cost delta by route
Low overhead: end-to-end CPU overhead for trace emission is <1% p99 of request latency for production traffic when sampling at 10%
Backwards compatible: traces can be ingested by existing trace pipeline without schema-breaking changes (fields appended or optional)
Tests: unit + e2e synthetic workload demonstrating correct crediting for single-request, batched-prefetch, and prefix-share scenarios
tasks: Design chronograph span model and tagging strategy (schema + sampling policy)
Instrument runtime: emit spans at subtoken emission boundaries with layer durations
Capture KV prefetch events and attach prefetch_tag to affected spans
Implement offline reconciler job to amortize prefetch costs and validate against live traces
Add Grafana dashboard panels and a lightweight request timeline explorer in Console
Add unit and integration tests (synthetic workloads and recorded traces)
Performance review and cost budget (10% sampling target)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): 1% sampling on staging + internal traffic, validate schema and overhead
Phase 2 (verification): 10% sampling on low-risk production routes for 2 weeks, run reconciler on recorded traces
Phase 3 (ramp): 25% sampling for non-latency-critical routes and enable dashboard alerts
Phase 4 (opt-in): enable for Dedicated tenants behind feature flag and provide guidance for Private deployments
testing_plan: Microbench harness: measure emission CPU and wall-time for different sampling rates
Synthetic scenarios: single-request prefetch, multi-request shared-prefix, high-batch-size stress tests
Integration: end-to-end ingestion into trace pipeline, validation job run to compare amortized costs vs ground truth
SLO guardrails: ensure no regression in 99th percentile latency for monitored routes
monitoring_dashboards: Console route dashboard: per-route chronograph sample rate and p95/p99 compute vs kv split
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: trace emission increases request latency under high qps. Mitigation: implement adaptive sampling and offload to async emitter
Risk: KV amortization model disagrees with billing pipeline. Mitigation: reconciliation job and shadow-run mode for 4 weeks before switching chargeback
Risk: schema churn breaks downstream consumers. Mitigation: add optional fields and maintain stable core keys; coordinate with telemetry team
